predictive_colour.reading: This is what carries the row, not the area. The magenta image and the green image change THE SAME PIXELS as each other and as the baseline -- frame by frame the counts and bounding boxes agree (8, 8, 7-8, 11 on the first four frames of the burst) -- and the MAGNITUDE tracks the colour distance: 77-229 of 765 for magenta against retail, 54-237 for green against retail, and up to 459 for magenta against green, which are the two furthest apart. A pixel set that moves with the value of a packed colour word is that colour word being painted. Nothing else has that signature.

witnesses.scope: Runtime-proved for the screens savestate K-01 reaches with no input, and no further, and small: the facemask and turtleneck words are drawn on 2 to 13 pixels per frame (median 5) at the camera distance this scene uses. The claim rests on the two-colour control, not on area: the same pixels change under both replacement colours and their magnitude tracks the colour distance, while a second same-length rebuild of the same image changes no pixel at all. Which record is drawn on which player is not claimed, and a closer camera would be needed to see the kit at any size.

coverage.why_fixed_allocation_decides: A fixed-allocation lane rewrites bytes in place and changes no member's stored size, so the disc read schedule is untouched and the two runs stay in lockstep; the comparison is then exact equality outside the edit. A re-packing lane moves stored sizes, which moves the read schedule, which the spec measured turning into a different scene 59 seconds downstream. This column is measured off each lane object's own fixed_allocation attribute [M], and it is the column that decides the order of work.
